title: Carving of the Great Sphinx of Giza
summary: The Great Sphinx was cut from the Giza plateau bedrock in the 4th Dynasty. Egypt's antiquities ministry attributes it to the reign of Khafre, c. 2558–2532 BCE, citing its position by his temples and its likeness to his statues. Workers left a block of limestone when quarrying the surrounding ditch.

uncertainty.note: Dating is by attribution to Khafre's reign; the source gives only the 4th Dynasty (c. 2613–2494 BC) for the carving itself.

as_recorded.value: Carved during the 4th Dynasty (c. 2613–2494 BC), in the reign of Khafre (c. 2558–2532 BC)

where.historical_name: Giza plateau beside the valley temple of Khafre, necropolis near Memphis, Old Kingdom Egypt (4th Dynasty)

importance.justification: The largest monumental sculpture of the Old Kingdom and an icon of ancient Egypt, carved directly out of the natural rock.
